content:
I mentioned in today's Siri AI Apple Watch article that there is one more change I'd like Apple to restore before watchOS 27 is officially released, which is expected to roll out this month. This feature is actually a muscle-memory operation that has been around for many years, and I've been finding it very inconvenient all summer without it.

In watchOS 27, double-clicking the Digital Crown can no longer be used to quickly switch between different apps

I already wrote this morning:

When Apple released the first public beta of watchOS 27 in July, I had already flagged this issue, and I had also relayed my feedback to Apple back in June.

Apple Watch has long had a hidden gesture that lets you quickly switch between two apps, or between a recently used app and the watch face.

I hadn't paid particular attention to this gesture for many years, but in fact I'd been using it all the time.

In watchOS 27, both single-clicking and double-clicking the Digital Crown bring up the dynamic app list

This feature was removed in watchOS 27 beta 1. The reason seems to be that Apple wants to heavily promote the new "dynamic app list" feature in watchOS 27. Now pressing the Digital Crown once shows Siri's app icon, plus five intelligently recommended app icons, plus an icon that lets you see the full app list.

After using it for a while, I'm starting to find the dynamic app list pretty decent. If the app you're looking for is already in the recommendations bar, it really is quite convenient.

But it still can't replace the clean, crisp operation of double-clicking the Digital Crown to instantly jump between apps. In watchOS 27, there's no longer any way to quickly switch apps this way. In the watchOS 27 beta, double-clicking the Digital Crown produces exactly the same result as a single click.

The old method is really handy for quickly jumping between apps like Workout and Music.

As I've mentioned before, the Apple Watch itself has very few physical buttons — only the Ultra model has the Action button. Given that, I think removing the double-click gesture from one of the buttons is a wrong decision.

Highlighted comment from Ben B

I've already submitted feedback through the Feedback app, because this change is simply bizarre. While typing up my feedback, I thought about the fact that no replacement was provided after this feature was removed, which makes me wonder if an upcoming new watch might reassign the double-click gesture to a different purpose, which is why the original function was pulled. Looks like I'll have to wait until next week to find out.

As for the side button below the Digital Crown, the double-click function remains unchanged: it's still used to open Apple Wallet cards. Hopefully the official version of watchOS 27 can restore the Digital Crown's double-click gesture, or at least bring it back in watchOS 27.1.

Do you use this gesture on your Apple Watch? Have you been missing it in the watchOS 27 beta? Will you find it inconvenient after upgrading? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
